notes:
Account background:
- Mid-size payments processor, heavy real-time chat + automated review pipelines.
- Primary concern: tail latency for high-value customer escalations; also cost predictability.

Technical requirements & priorities:
- Must run on Dedicated with VPC peering. No shared-host for priority flows.
- Tenant isolation: want dedicated logical pools per product line (support/chat vs fraud rerank).
- Priority lanes: 3 tiers (priority=escalation, standard=chat, background=batch rerank). Priority lanes must guarantee p95/p99 SLOs for priority flows.
- Per-route quotas: route-level reserved concurrency + burst bucket. Need hard caps to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: preemption for priority lanes, GPU soft isolation (shares + cgroups), and per-tenant KV cache limits.
- Routing & fallbacks: auto-fallback to lower-cost model variant when capacity constrained; but for priority lane, must not fallback without explicit allow.
- Observability: token-level latency and cost breakdown, per-route tracing, and per-lane SLA dashboards.

Performance targets requested:
- Target SLOs: priority p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms; standard p95 < 250ms.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 250 req/s for priority lane (avg payload ~40 tokens), burst to 1000 req/s for 30s.
- Reserved GPU ask: initial plan 16 x A100 (or 8 x H100 equivalent) across 2 AZs; 2-GPU hot spare pool for failover.
- Acceptance criteria for POC: demonstrate isolation (no cross-route latency degradation under noisy load), meet p95/p99 for priority flows, show autoscaling triggers and graceful preemption.

Commercial & negotiation notes:
- CTO quote: "We can't tolerate tail latency spikes for premium customers. SLA must include measurable remedies."
- Procurement pushing for credit/fee language on missed SLOs. Legal wants clearer definition of 'throughput guarantees' (tokens vs requests).
